title: Fluid Layouts
definition: Layouts built using relative units (like `%`, `vw`, `fr`) instead of fixed units (`px`), allowing elements to smoothly expand and contract with the browser window.
simpleExplanation: Instead of saying 'This box is exactly 500px wide' and hoping the user's screen is bigger than 500px, you say 'This box takes up 50% of the screen'. As the user stretches their browser, the box stretches with it like rubber.
realWorldExample: Using CSS Grid with `1fr 2fr`. The layout is fluid because the columns are mathematical fractions, not rigid pixels.
useCases: Handling the infinite variety of Android screen sizes

basic: Which unit creates a more fluid layout: `px` or `%`?
intermediate: How do you prevent a fluid layout from stretching too far on a massive 4K monitor?

answers.question: px or %?
answers.answer: `%` (Percentages). It recalculates its size constantly based on the parent container.

answers.question: Prevent over-stretching?
answers.answer: Use the `max-width` property. E.g., `width: 100%; max-width: 1200px;`. It will be fully fluid on phones and laptops, but stop stretching once it hits 1200px on a giant TV.

codeExample:
I am a RIGID box (600px). Shrink your browser very small and watch me break your screen!
I am a FLUID box (80%). I adapt to your screen size instantly. Stretch the screen really wide, and I stop at 800px!
